newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hengyun says interim net fell 32 pct.
newsitem.headline: Hengyun says interim net fell 32 pct.

text.p: Shenzhen-listed Guangzhou Hengyun Heat and Power Co Ltd said 1996 interim net profits dove 31.92 percent from 21.97 million yuan in the first half of 1995.

Under Chinese accounting standards, Hengyun had after-tax profits of 14.95 million yuan in the January-June period of this year, the company said in an interim report published in the Shenzhen Securities Times.
Main operating income hit 264.47 million yuan against 265.91 million yuan in the first two quarters of 1995.
The firm said lower earnings was due to a 15 percent rise in the price of coal, which fuels most of its power generators.

A company spokesman recently blamed the lower first-half earnings on an oversupply of electricity in Guangdong province in the first six months of this year, which forced Hengyun to reduce its output of electricity.

The official said Hengyun expects its earnings to pick up in the second half of this year, fueled by an anticipated strengthening of demand for electricity and a raising of the government's caps on power rates.
Hengyun aims to chalk up 40 million yuan in after-tax profits for the whole of 1996, compared with 29.74 million yuan posted the previous year, the official said.
